answer:
**Interleaving compares rankers within a shared result impression.** Team-draft interleaving alternates selections from two ranked lists, randomizes the starting side, and avoids duplicates. Clicks are attributed to the ranker that contributed each item, yielding a preference signal. [1](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2010/07/fp146-radlinski.pdf)

Sharing one impression can reduce some noise from comparing separate user groups. It is especially useful when the question is which ranking users prefer. However, attribution rules, position effects, and ranker similarity influence sensitivity.

**Shadow traffic answers a different question.** A candidate system runs on real requests without showing its results. This reveals latency, errors, and output differences, but users cannot react to an output they never see, so it does not estimate its causal engagement effect.

Use shadowing for operational readiness, interleaving for suitable relative ranking comparisons, and randomized A/B tests for downstream business outcomes and guardrails. There is no universal ten-to-fifty-times speedup. Match the experiment to the claim you want to make rather than treating all online evaluations as interchangeable.

**Technical details and references.**

Team-draft interleaving alternates between two rankers' result lists, randomizes the initial team, avoids duplicate results, and attributes subsequent clicks to the contributing ranker. Comparing preferences within a shared impression can be more sensitive than comparing independent traffic groups for ranking changes. [1](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2010/07/fp146-radlinski.pdf)

It is not a universal 10–50-fold speedup: sensitivity depends on ranker differences, click noise, attribution, and the metric. Interleaving mainly estimates relative ranking preference, not every business impact. Shadow traffic runs a candidate without showing its output, revealing latency/errors and offline differences but not the user's causal response. Use shadowing for operational checks, interleaving for suitable ranking comparisons, and randomized A/B tests for downstream outcomes and guardrails.
